methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units based on individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit is designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. This ensures a granular comparison between the two information sources.
mindtraced_atomic_units: FSM acts as an arbiter circuit for three devices.
Resetn is active-low synchronous and resets to state A.
FSM stays in state A when no requests are active (r[1]=0, r[2]=0, r[3]=0).
If r[1]=1 in state A, transition to B (g[1]=1).
If r[1]=0 and r[2]=1 in state A, transition to C (g[2]=1).
If r[1]=0, r[2]=0, and r[3]=1 in state A, transition to D (g[3]=1).
If r[1]=0, r[2]=0, and r[3]=0 in state A, stay in A.
If r[1]=1 in state B, stay in B (g[1]=1).
If r[1]=0 in state B, transition to A.
If r[2]=1 in state C, stay in C (g[2]=1).
If r[2]=0 in state C, transition to A.
If r[3]=1 in state D, stay in D (g[3]=1).
If r[3]=0 in state D, transition to A.
Use separate always blocks for state table and flip-flops.
Describe outputs g[i] using continuous assignment or always block.
spec_atomic_units: Module top_module has inputs clk, resetn, r[3:1], and outputs g[3:1].
Module represents an arbiter FSM.
r[3:1] are request signals from three devices.
g[3:1] are grant signals to those devices.
clk is the clock signal.
resetn is the active-low synchronous reset signal.
Combinational logic determines g[3:1] based on current state and r[3:1].
FSM implements a priority arbitration scheme (device 1 > device 2 > device 3).
Idle State (State A): If no requests are active, FSM remains in State A, and all grant signals are deasserted.
Priority Encoding: When one or more requests are active, the combinational logic must determine which device receives the grant based on the priority scheme.
Grant Persistence: Once a device is granted access (g[i] == 1), it continues to receive the grant as long as its request signal remains asserted (r[i] == 1).
If the request is deasserted (r[i] == 0), the FSM transitions back to the idle state.
State A (Idle): If r[1] == 0 && r[2] == 0 && r[3] == 0: Remain in State A, g[1] = 0, g[2] = 0, g[3] = 0.
State A (Idle): If r[1] == 1: Transition to State B, g[1] = 1, g[2] = 0, g[3] = 0.
State A (Idle): If r[1] == 0 && r[2] == 1: Transition to State C, g[1] = 0, g[2] = 1, g[3] = 0.
State A (Idle): If r[1] == 0 && r[2] == 0 && r[3] == 1: Transition to State D, g[1] = 0, g[2] = 0, g[3] = 1.
State B (Device 1 Granted): g[1] = 1, g[2] = 0, g[3] = 0.
State B (Device 1 Granted): If r[1] == 0: Transition to State A.
State B (Device 1 Granted): If r[1] == 1: Remain in State B.
State C (Device 2 Granted): g[1] = 0, g[2] = 1, g[3] = 0.
State C (Device 2 Granted): If r[2] == 0: Transition to State A.
State C (Device 2 Granted): If r[2] == 1: Remain in State C.
State D (Device 3 Granted): g[1] = 0, g[2] = 0, g[3] = 1.
State D (Device 3 Granted): If r[3] == 0: Transition to State A.
State D (Device 3 Granted): If r[3] == 1: Remain in State D.
g[1] = current_state == B || (current_state == A && r[1]);
g[2] = current_state == C || (current_state == A && r[1] == 0 && r[2]);
g[3] = current_state == D || (current_state == A && r[1] == 0 && r[2] == 0 && r[3]);
resetn is an active-low synchronous reset. When resetn is low, the FSM should transition to state A, and all grant signals should be deasserted.
FSM's state transitions occur on the rising edge of the clk signal.
The resetn signal, when low, synchronously resets the FSM to its initial state (state A) on the rising edge of clk.
The grants g are asserted based on the current state, which is updated on the rising edge of clk.
The FSM will have at least one register to store the current state.
The state transitions are determined by the combinational logic based on the current state and the inputs r.
The state register is updated using non-blocking assignments (<=) within an always @(posedge clk) block.
The reset is synchronous, meaning it only takes effect on the rising edge of the clock when resetn is low.
